regulatory_mandate.primary: PSR PS23/3 — APP Fraud Mandatory Reimbursement (in force 7 October 2024)
secondary: Payment Systems Act 2013 — PSR enforcement powers
FPS Scheme Rules (Pay.UK) — receiving PSP obligations
FCA Consumer Duty — consumer support outcome (non-deterrence of legitimate claims)
PSR SD17 — Confirmation of Payee (evidential context for gross negligence assessment)

sub_flow_1.name: Real-time Detection
sub_flow_1.description: Fraud scoring during JRN-002 (Faster Payment Initiation) is the prevention layer. JRN-005 sub-flow 1 picks up when a payment is blocked by SVC-013 (fraud_risk_level = block) OR when a customer reports fraud after the fact. No financial loss occurs on the real-time block path — the case is created for pattern learning and ML model feedback.
sub_flow_1.primary_outcome: Payment blocked — no loss. Fraud case opened for analyst review and ML pattern feedback.

sub_flow_2.name: Post-payment Investigation and Reimbursement
sub_flow_2.description: Customer reports they were socially engineered into making a payment to a fraudster. Fraud analyst investigates the original payment record, device data, and communication logs. Reimbursement decision made within 5 business days. Reimbursement credited to customer account. 50% recovery claim raised against receiving PSP via Pay.UK mechanism.
sub_flow_2.primary_outcome: Customer reimbursed up to £85,000 within 5 business days. Recovery claim raised against receiving PSP.

phases.description: The fraud journey is initiated by one of two triggers: (1) Real-time block — SVC-013 publishes PaymentFraudBlocked (EVT-186) during JRN-002 execution. The payment is prevented; no funds leave the account. SVC-013 creates a draft FraudCase with trigger_type = realtime_block. (2) Customer report — PER-001 contacts the bank via mobile app (CH-002) or telephone (CH-004) to report they believe they have been victim of APP fraud. Customer Service Agent (PER-056) logs the report; SVC-013 creates a FraudCase with trigger_type = customer_report.

trigger_conditions.name: Real-time Block
trigger_conditions.description: SVC-013 scored the payment as fraud_risk_level = block during JRN-002. SVC-001 published PaymentFraudBlocked. SVC-013 consumes this event and creates a FraudCase for pattern learning and analyst review.

trigger_conditions.name: Customer Report — Mobile App
trigger_conditions.description: PER-001 navigates to 'Report Fraud' section of mobile app. Selects the suspect transaction from their payment history. Completes in-app fraud report form. SVC-017 calls SVC-013 POST /fraud-cases.

trigger_conditions.name: Customer Report — Telephone
trigger_conditions.description: PER-001 calls the bank's fraud reporting line. Customer Service Agent (PER-056) authenticates caller via voice biometrics / security questions. Agent creates FraudCase via SVC-013 case management UI.

phases.sla: FraudCase must be created within 4 hours of customer report (GOV-003-R01 complaint handling)

phases.description: A Fraud Analyst (PER-054) is assigned to the case from the fraud operations queue. The analyst retrieves the original PaymentIntent (ENT-008) and PaymentExecution (ENT-009) records. Device data, session logs, and CoP result are gathered as initial evidence. A FraudEvidence record is created for each evidence item. The case status transitions to investigating.
activities: Retrieve PaymentIntent record from SVC-001 — confirms payment amount, payee details, CoP result, cop_override_confirmed, fraud_score, fraud_risk_level
Retrieve PaymentExecution record from SVC-009 — confirms fps_reference, settlement status, receiving sort code
Retrieve device data and session metadata from SVC-017 (Digital Channels) — IP address, device fingerprint, behavioural biometrics at time of payment
Retrieve communication log — in-app and email warnings presented to customer before payment authorisation
Create FraudEvidence records for each evidence type
Assign case to analyst; set FraudCase.status = investigating
Publish FraudInvestigationStarted event
phases.sla: Case assigned to analyst within 4 hours of FraudCaseCreated

phases.description: The Fraud Analyst conducts a full investigation, reviewing all available evidence against the PSR PS23/3 eligibility criteria. Key investigative questions: (1) Did the customer ignore explicit fraud warnings? (2) Did the CoP return a no_match that was overridden without reasonable justification? (3) Is there evidence the customer was acting in concert with the fraudster (professional fraud)? (4) Is the customer a vulnerable consumer requiring additional support? (5) Are there mule network indicators at the receiving sort code? The analyst also checks if a SAR referral is required to the MLRO (PER-052).

psr_eligibility_criteria: Customer did not act with gross negligence (ignored explicit warnings, proceeded with no_match CoP without justification)
Customer is not the perpetrator of the fraud
Claim is within the 13-month reporting window
Payment was a Faster Payment (FPS) covered by the scheme
gross_negligence_indicators: cop_result = no_match AND cop_override_confirmed = true with no additional vulnerability factors
Customer ignored an explicit fraud warning modal at payment execution
Customer provided false information in the fraud report
Customer refused to co-operate with the investigation
investigation_framework.vulnerability_assessment: Mandatory for all cases. PSR PS23/3 requires extra care for vulnerable consumers. A vulnerability flag elevates the standard — gross negligence threshold is higher for confirmed vulnerable customers.
investigation_framework.mule_network_check: Analyst checks the receiving sort code and account number against Cifas National Fraud Database and internal mule account indicators. If the receiving account is at this bank, the account is flagged for immediate review by a separate team (EX-006 exception path).
investigation_framework.sar_referral_trigger: If investigation reveals organised fraud network, professional fraudster, or internal collusion — MLRO (PER-052) is notified for SAR consideration under POCA 2002 s330

phases.sla: Investigation must complete within 4 business days to allow time for reimbursement within the 5-day PSR SLA

phases.description: The Fraud Analyst (or Senior Manager PER-059 for high-value or gross negligence cases) records the formal reimbursement decision. Three outcomes are possible: (1) Approve — full reimbursement up to £85,000. (2) Partial — contributory negligence applies; reimbursement reduced by a documented percentage. (3) Decline — gross negligence with documented evidence that meets the PSR standard of proof. The decision must be communicated to the customer within 5 business days of the original report via a regulated outcome letter.

responsible_personas.high_value_or_gross_negligence: PER-059 (Senior Manager) — mandatory escalation for any case where: (a) reimbursement amount > £25,000, or (b) decision is Decline on gross negligence grounds

decision_outcomes.description: Customer is eligible for full reimbursement. No gross negligence. No evidence of fraud by customer. Reimbursement amount = min(total_loss_amount, 85000). FraudCase.status transitions to reimbursed after credit is applied.
decision_outcomes.regulatory_note: Default outcome under PSR PS23/3. Bank must reimburse unless it can demonstrate gross negligence to the PSR standard.

decision_outcomes.description: Contributory negligence applies. Customer contributed to the loss (e.g. overrode a no_match CoP warning but is not fully grossly negligent due to vulnerability factors). Reimbursement amount < total_loss_amount. Documented percentage split with justification.
decision_outcomes.regulatory_note: PSR PS23/3 allows partial reimbursement where contributory negligence is established. Evidence must be documented and proportionate.

decision_outcomes.description: Gross negligence established with documented evidence meeting the PSR standard of proof. FraudCase.status transitions to declined. Customer must be provided a clear written explanation and signposted to the Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS). Evidence retained in FraudCase.gross_negligence_evidence.
decision_outcomes.regulatory_note: PSR PS23/3 — gross negligence is a high bar. The bank bears the burden of proof. FOS appeal is available to the customer. Decision must be documented to support FOS case review.

phases.description: For approved and partial decisions: SVC-001 (Retail Banking Core) credits the reimbursement amount to the customer's account. The credit is sourced from the bank's APP fraud loss account (internal suspense account). A ReimbursementClaim record is created by SVC-009 to track the 50/50 cost split against the receiving PSP. The claim is submitted to the receiving PSP via Pay.UK's reimbursement mechanism. The customer is notified via push notification and email.
phases.responsible_service: SVC-001 for account credit; SVC-009 for ReimbursementClaim creation and submission
activities: SVC-001 receives FraudReimbursementApproved event. Credits FraudCase.reimbursement_amount to Account.account_id.
SVC-001 debits APP fraud loss suspense account by same amount.
SVC-009 creates ReimbursementClaim record: sending_bank_share = reimbursement_amount * 0.5, receiving_bank_share = reimbursement_amount * 0.5.
SVC-009 submits recovery claim to receiving PSP via Pay.UK reimbursement API.
SVC-053 (Notification Service) dispatches push notification and email to PER-001 confirming credit and amount.
Publish ReimbursementCredited event (SVC-001).
Publish RecoveryInitiated event (SVC-009).
outputs: Recovery claim submitted to receiving PSP
phases.sla: Credit must appear in customer account within 5 business days of original fraud report (PSR PS23/3 GOV-003-R01)

phases.description: SVC-009 manages the recovery of funds from the receiving PSP. The receiving PSP has a symmetric obligation under PSR PS23/3 to cooperate with the sending PSP's recovery claim. Outcomes: Full recovery (receiving PSP returns 50% share), Partial recovery, or Failed (receiving PSP disputes liability, mule account empty). For disputed claims, the bank can escalate to Pay.UK scheme dispute resolution. Recovery does not affect the customer's reimbursement — the customer has already been credited.
activities: Receiving PSP responds to recovery claim (typically within 15 business days under scheme rules).
SVC-009 updates ReimbursementClaim.recovery_status and recovery_amount.
If full recovery: bank recoup 50% of paid reimbursement. Publish RecoveryCompleted event.
If partial recovery: partial recoup recorded. ReimbursementClaim.recovery_status = partial.
If failed: receiving PSP disputes, mule account empty, or receiving PSP in administration. ReimbursementClaim.recovery_status = failed. Escalate to Pay.UK dispute mechanism.
Receiving PSP dispute: senior manager review for Pay.UK scheme escalation.
outputs: RecoveryCompleted or final recovery outcome event published
phases.note: Recovery timeline is independent of the 5-day customer reimbursement SLA. Customer is reimbursed regardless of recovery outcome.

phases.description: The Fraud Analyst records the final case outcome. FraudCase.status transitions to closed. The fraud pattern indicators from this case are fed back to SVC-013's ML model via a FraudPatternDetected event — this closes the loop between investigation outcomes and real-time detection accuracy. The PSR quarterly regulatory reporting counter is incremented. If a SAR was raised, the MLRO is notified of case closure.
activities: Record final case outcome and recovery result.
Publish FraudPatternDetected event — payload contains anonymised pattern features (payee sort code patterns, social engineering typology, device indicators) as ML model training input to SVC-013.
Update PSR quarterly reporting counter (claims volume, reimbursement total, decline rate, recovery rate).
Notify MLRO (PER-052) of closure if SAR was raised in PH-066.
Set FraudCase.status = closed.
Publish FraudCaseClosed event.
Archive case record to WORM store (SVC-111) — 7-year retention.

happy_path.description: Customer reports APP fraud via mobile app → FraudCase created (trigger_type = customer_report) → Fraud Analyst assigned within 4 hours → Investigation completed within 4 business days → Reimbursement approved (full) → Customer account credited within 5 business days → ReimbursementClaim raised against receiving PSP → Recovery attempted → Case closed → Pattern fed back to ML model.

alternative_paths.name: Real-time Block — No Financial Loss
alternative_paths.description: Payment is blocked in JRN-002 (fraud_risk_level = block). FraudCase created with trigger_type = realtime_block and total_loss_amount = 0. Customer is notified of the blocked payment in the mobile app. Fraud Analyst reviews the case for pattern quality and false-positive assessment. No reimbursement required. Case closed; FraudPatternDetected event published.

alternative_paths.name: Partial Reimbursement — Contributory Negligence
alternative_paths.description: Investigation establishes that the customer overrode a CoP no_match warning but is not fully grossly negligent (e.g. elderly customer with vulnerability indicators). Decision = partial reimbursement. Reimbursement amount documented with percentage justification. ReimbursementClaim raised for the partial amount. Customer receives outcome letter explaining the contributory negligence finding and FOS signpost.

exception_paths.name: Gross Negligence Decline
exception_paths.description: Investigation establishes gross negligence to the PSR standard (e.g. customer ignored multiple explicit fraud warnings, overrode no_match CoP without vulnerability factors, provided false claim details). Decision = decline. gross_negligence_evidence documented and immutably stored. Outcome letter dispatched within 5 business days with clear explanation and FOS signpost. Senior Manager (PER-059) must co-sign the decline. Case escalated to Senior Manager for sign-off before outcome letter is issued.
exception_paths.regulatory_note: PSR PS23/3 — bank bears burden of proof for gross negligence. FOS receives a significant volume of APP fraud complaints. Evidence must be complete and proportionate.

exception_paths.name: Receiving PSP Disputes Liability
exception_paths.description: Receiving PSP contests the 50/50 cost split, claiming the sending bank failed to perform adequate fraud controls. SVC-009 escalates the ReimbursementClaim to Pay.UK scheme dispute resolution. Senior Manager (PER-059) authorises the dispute submission. Timeline extends beyond standard recovery window. Customer is unaffected — reimbursement has already been credited.

exception_paths.name: Repeat Victim — Enhanced Vulnerability Assessment
exception_paths.description: PER-001 has submitted a previous APP fraud claim within 12 months. Mandatory enhanced vulnerability assessment performed before proceeding to standard investigation. MLRO (PER-052) notified. Investigation considers whether this bank's safeguards are adequate for this customer's vulnerability level. If confirmed vulnerable: standard gross negligence threshold does not apply; full reimbursement subject only to fraud-by-customer exclusion.

exception_paths.name: Mule Account Detected at This Bank
exception_paths.description: Investigation reveals that the receiving account is held at this bank (identified via the receiving sort code matching the bank's own sort code range). The receiving account is an internal mule. This triggers a separate financial crime investigation by the MLRO (PER-052). The receiving account is immediately frozen (Account.status = frozen). SAR is raised to NCA UKFIU. The fraud case proceeds to reimbursement on the normal timeline — the internal mule account investigation is parallel.
exception_paths.parallel_process: JRN-003 (SAR Filing) is triggered in parallel

exception_paths.name: Stop-the-Clock — Suspected Fraud-by-Customer
exception_paths.description: During investigation, the Fraud Analyst identifies indicators that the customer may have made the payment knowingly and is making a false claim. The PSR allows the 5-business-day clock to be stopped pending further investigation. Senior Manager (PER-059) must authorise the stop-the-clock decision. Customer must be notified that additional time is needed. If fraud-by-customer is established: case declined with full documentation; referral to Action Fraud.
